summary: Hold. The conjecture is that bf16 master's 'newer' swap-AB kernel will run in decode at its standalone 9.7/3.9 us. That premise is false, and the transfer has already been measured: the qkv/o kernel and configs at m<=16 are byte-identical to what qkv-o-swapab16-t2-t16-no-fork ran (job b0057d2e6cef4d5a), where the same kernels measured qkv 12.7-13.0 us and o 6.2-6.5 us in context, and sliding verify_1/decode_16 were flat. The genuinely new cells (sliding decode_1 T=1, T=32, unpooler T=16/32) project to about -1..-2.5 us per shape (~0.3-0.6% geomean), which a scored submit cannot resolve; bf16_proj already measured the T=16 full unpooler cell as a regression.
justification: A. MECHANISM: swap-AB at m<=32 is real on H100/H200 (wgmma m64n16/n32 instead of mma.sync), and it removes cuBLAS's splitKreduce node (1.8 us in decode). bf16_proj does measure _bf16_swapab_kernel at qkv 9.5-9.8 us (m=1/8/16) and 11.6 (m=32), and o 3.9-4.7 us (pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256.result.json). BUT THE TRANSFER HAS ALREADY BEEN MEASURED, and it fails: decode's qkv-o-swapab16-t2-t16-no-fork ran the identical kernel. git diff b99b1dd3..master on muse_bf16_proj/submission.py touches only the unpooler-slice / ouns routing; SWAPAB16_CFG qkv (2304,8192,SK4,BK128,4st), o (8192,1024,SK1,BK256,4st), BLOCK_T=WS_M=16 and _bf16_swapab_kernel are unchanged, so the 'newer kernel rather than re-running qkv-o-swapab16's code' claim is false at T<=16. Its profile (archive/qkv-o-swapab16-t2-t16-no-fork/b0057d2e6cef4d5a.profile.txt) shows _swapab_qkv_kernel at 12.7-13.0 us vs nvjet 128x8/64x16 splitK at 12.0-12.6 + splitKreduce 1.8 us, a saving of ~1-1.5 us, not ~4.5. _swapab_o_kernel ran at 6.2-6.5 us vs nvjet 64x8 at 6.6-7.0, a saving of ~0.5 us, not ~3. Decode's own prepare-time graph selector in that run (log lines 119/180) saw qkv T8+T16 40.6 vs 43.3 us (1.066x) and o 24.7 vs 24.8 (1.004x, which would be OFF under this hypothesis's 1.02x rule). Result: sliding verify_1 191.58 vs 191.42 (flat), sliding decode_16 204.72 vs 204.68 (flat). The Triton kernel loses ~3 us (qkv) and ~2.3 us (o) in decode relative to bf16_proj's rows, while nvjet does not. The cause is unidentified, but it is reproducible. PER-CELL REALISTIC EXPECTATION with that context penalty: sliding decode_1 T=1 qkv ~12.7 vs 13.8 (nvjet+reduce), o ~6.3 vs 7.0, so ~-1.5..-2 us on 118 us (~1.5%, inside the ~1.5% noise). T=8/16: already measured flat (duplicate). T=32: qkv ~14 vs 12.2-12.6+1.8, o ~7 vs its share of the 26.4-27.7 us 2-call row, so ~-1 us on 239/431 us (0.2-0.4%). Unpooler T=32: bf16 itself shows 18.8 swap-AB vs ~18.5 nvjet (no win even standalone). Unpooler T=16: bf16_proj ran exactly this cell (unpooler-full-m16-swapab-route, done/regression: 18.51 vs 18.48 flat, others lost), and bf16 master deliberately keeps cuBLAS for the full unpooler at 9..16. So 'copy verbatim from master' and 'route the unpooler at 9..16' contradict each other. The 'expected' block (-7 us decode_1, -6 us verify_1, -4..-7 decode_16, -3..-6 decode_32) overstates the measured transfer by roughly 3-5x. WEAKEST LINK: the selector is the hypothesis's only guard against in-context loss, and it times the GEMM in isolation (graph replay + 256 MB flush), which is close to bf16_proj's conditions. It therefore cannot see the context penalty that sank the earlier port: its qkv cell would be ON again for the same flat shape result. CONFIRM/REFUTE: a scored run cannot read a ~0.3-0.6% geomean move. The kernel rows can be read, but for T<=16 they are already known.
confounders: qkv-o-swapab16-t2-t16-no-fork (not landed, neutral/unproven-vs-best, job b0057d2e6cef4d5a): same kernel, same qkv/o configs, same call sites at T=2..16. It is the direct prior measurement, and this run would re-measure it at T=8/16 (identical code at those cells).

dense-chain-s3-t1-q-sk2-o-route-unpool + dl3-piece-a-gate-stride-check-fix: piece A owns qkv/o at full decode_1, and piece C owns the unpooler at T<=8. If piece A falls back at prepare, as it did in b0057d2e's log, the full decode_1 cell moves too, so read full decode_1 only together with the [dl3] PATH CHOSEN line. Otherwise this run does not confound them; the gates are disjoint by design.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: P/R run as a PDL chain at T<=32 right after the attention boundary. A non-PDL Triton o kernel ahead of that chain can cost the overlap nvjet gives. This is one plausible part of the measured ~2-3 us in-context penalty, but unverified.

full-decode-sk-ticket-restack / splitkv: these produce o at full decode_16/32 as a reshape of the sk output. The layout is warmed in prepare in the earlier port. No new interaction beyond the one above.
interference: No companion would rescue interpretability. The binding problem is not interference with a landed change. The effect of the new cells (~1-2 us on 118-431 us shapes) is below per-shape noise, and the T<=16 cells repeat a measured-flat result. A control (e.g. a qkv-only or T=1-only cell) would cost a second scored run to read a sub-noise effect. If this is re-minted, the right fix is in-prepare rather than a companion. (1) Time each cell IN CONTEXT: capture kernel_fn (or _parent_attention plus the following boundary/P launch) for that T with the flag on and off, interleave the replays, and gate on >=1.02x of the whole captured segment, not the isolated GEMM. That is the only selector that can see the penalty seen in b0057d2e. (2) Restrict to cells not yet measured: sliding decode_1 T=1 qkv/o and T=32 qkv/o. Drop T=8/16 (duplicate), drop unpooler T=16 (bf16 regression) and unpooler T=32 (no standalone win). (3) Fix the expected block to -1..-2 us per shape. That version is best folded into a combination round rather than spending a standalone scored submit.
rules_flags: None blocking. The design keeps kernel_fn free of syncs, prints, try/except and per-call mutable state. Gates are cfg/shape plus prepare-time per-state flags. Workspaces and self-resetting tickets are per state. No process-global flag (BLAS backend / cuBLASLt preference) is set or restored per call, and none is needed.

Builder note: bf16 master's _swapab_forward / _swapab16_forward take a report=True branch containing try/except. Keep that only on the prepare path, as the earlier port did, so kernel_fn's call graph has no try/except.

_swapab_route_ok in bf16 reads cfg['m'/'n'/'k']. Decode's cfg has 'tokens', not 'm'. Adapt the gate to cfg['tokens'] and constant shapes; do not key it on x.shape alone if that differs from config semantics.
open_questions: Why does the identical _bf16_swapab_kernel run ~3 us slower in decode (12.7-13.0 vs 9.5-9.8 for qkv; 6.2-6.5 vs 3.9-4.2 for o) while nvjet stays near its standalone time? Candidates: bf16_proj's profile leaves the 37.7 MB qkv weight partly L2-resident across reps (decode's preceding kernels evict it); loss of PDL/launch overlap next to the dense chain; or SM clocks under the layer's Marlin/attention load. Until this is explained, no bf16_proj Triton GEMM row should be used as a decode expectation.

Does decode's sliding decode_1 still run nvjet 128x8 splitK + splitKreduce for qkv on current master 6773ec5c (the BEST profile's top-3 no longer shows it)? If yes, T=1 sliding is the one untested cell worth ~1.5-2 us.
If a re-mint is wanted, should it be the T=1-sliding + T=32 qkv-only slice, gated by an in-context whole-segment selector, folded into a combination submit?
